Classification and direction guard: all three edges assert association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true) at SYSTEMIC_INFLAMMATORY. Both systemic-disease edges state the REVERSE ARROW openly: in every located design the systemic disease is the antecedent and the ocular manifestation is the consequent, so the clinically operative arrow runs rheumatoid-arthritis or systemic-lupus-erythematosus to scleritis and these edges are the reciprocal view. The rank 1 uveitis edge adopts rather than disputes the international registry's own reservation that uveitis is an EXTENSION OF THE INFLAMMATORY PROCESS rather than a true structural complication, which is the reason that edge cannot be causal. The rank 3 edge is registered at explicitly LOWER evidential density than the rank 2 edge, because no located anchor reports a pair-specific effect estimate for the lupus pairing, and that difference is carried on the face of the edge rather than smoothed over.

Withheld routes and duplicate-scope screen: no glaucoma and no cataracts edge (DUPLICATE-SCOPE - the registry already carries direct uveitis-to-glaucoma and uveitis-to-cataracts edges, and this file's rank 1 uveitis edge is authored in the same batch, so authoring either would register the same route twice at different indirection and add a direct-versus-chain redundancy conflict to the standing CRG review set, even though the same registry names these the most frequent complications of scleritis at 102 complications in 58 of 154 patients); no peripheral ulcerative keratitis edge (recorded here rather than authored, because the catalog's keratitis identity is generic and does not distinguish the peripheral ulcerative form, and the located registry treats peripheral ulcerative keratitis as an extension of the inflammatory process on the same footing as uveitis, so a separate edge would add indirection without adding information); no dry-eye edge (TARGET-EXHAUSTION and MISSING IDENTITY - the rheumatoid-ocular review names dry eye disease the most frequent ocular manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis, but the catalog carries no dry-eye identity of its own and dry-eye-syndrome already appears in the registry under a different primary); and no granulomatosis with polyangiitis edge (SCOPE - the registry reports it as carrying the significantly highest rate of ocular complications at p<0.0001, but it is registered as an alternative etiology to rule out on all three edges rather than authored as a fifth route, since the target identity already carries multiple incoming edges from a different disease family).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Concomitant uveitis is the best-documented ocular companion of scleritis, and the largest located registry quantifies it both as a marker of more severe disease and as the single strongest predictor of structural complications: the AutoInflammatory Disease Alliance Network scleritis registry reports 154 patients with 218 eyes of non-infectious scleritis, records 102 ocular complications in 58 patients across 87 eyes, finds the most frequent complications to be cataract, scleral and corneal thinning, and glaucoma or increased ocular pressure, and reports that ocular complications were significantly more frequent among patients with granulomatosis with polyangiitis (p<0.0001) and with CONCOMITANT UVEITIS (p=0.023) (PMID 42105127); a population-based United Kingdom analysis of 10,939,823 patients with 2,946 incident scleritis cases characterises scleritis as a disease defined by its associations with infectious and immune-mediated inflammatory disease (PMID 33728815); and a single-centre cohort of 69 patients with 96 eyes reports non-infectious scleritis in 56 eyes (58.3 percent) against 40 eyes (41.7 percent) presumed infectious, with idiopathic disease and spondyloarthropathy common in the non-infectious group and tuberculosis-associated disease predominating in the presumed infectious group, and with the authors stressing the need for careful etiologic evaluation in tuberculosis-endemic settings (PMID 42377600); recorded as documented association only, with the registry's own definitional reservation carried openly rather than argued around.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the largest anchor explicitly declines to treat the relationship as a complication at all: the scleritis registry states that uveitis and peripheral ulcerative keratitis were considered EXTENSIONS OF THE INFLAMMATORY PROCESS rather than true structural complications, which is a definitional choice that this edge adopts rather than disputes, meaning the located evidence treats uveitis as a concurrent expression of the same disease rather than a consequence of scleritis. The reported association is therefore not a temporal sequence, and the p=0.023 figure describes how often complications occur in eyes that already carry concomitant uveitis, not what fraction of uveitis follows scleritis. The population-based anchor supplies the association structure but its located abstract does not report uveitis-specific incidence, and the Indonesian cohort is explicitly limited by its retrospective design, incomplete follow-up, and limited microbiological confirmation, with a high proportion of tuberculosis-associated cases that constrains generalisation. Individual claims require a dated ophthalmology assessment documenting uveitis independently, with slit-lamp or anterior-segment OCT evidence and an infectious workup separating non-infectious from tuberculosis-associated or other presumed infectious disease, since the located cohort shows the infectious proportion is not negligible even in a non-endemic-pattern clinic.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a shared scleritis-to-uvea inflammatory process rather than a lesion spreading from one tissue to another: scleritis is inflammation of the sclera and uveitis is inflammation of the uveal tract, and the located registry groups the two as extensions of a single inflammatory process occupying adjacent coats of the globe, so the proposed route is a common immune driver producing inflammation in both tissues simultaneously, with the same phenomenon expressed at two depths; the vector is named as simultaneous rather than sequential precisely because the anchor's own framing is simultaneous, and whether an individual's uveitis preceded, followed, or accompanied the scleral inflammation remains hypothesized until the two are separately dated.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at international-registry, population-based-cohort, and single-terre-centre-cohort class following the file's existing otologic, audiologic, visual, and treatment-related pathway scope: the registry is the only located source that quantifies the relationship and is registered together with its explicit definition of uveitis as an extension of the inflammatory process rather than a complication, because that definition is the reason the edge cannot be causal (PMID 42105127); the population-based anchor of 10,939,823 patients is the only located design that is not referral-selected and is therefore the anchor that supplies the association structure free of referral bias (PMID 33728815); and the Indonesian cohort is registered for the infectious-versus-non-infectious split, which is the located evidence that a proportion of scleritis is infectious and therefore that uveitis attribution must follow etiologic evaluation (PMID 42377600). Because the relationship is definitional-as-much-as-causal, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, adopts the registry's framing in the causation status, and requires dated separate documentation of each condition with infectious workup before any individual attribution.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The primary anchor is a 154-patient international registry of NON-INFECTIOUS scleritis only, so it cannot speak to the infectious half of the disease; its uveitis comparison is a subgroup contrast within that registry at p=0.023, a modest threshold, and the abstract does not report the absolute count of uveitis patients; the population-based anchor of 10,939,823 patients and 2,946 incident scleritis cases supplies the strongest denominator in this edge, but its located abstract reports the study design and adjustment set rather than uveitis-specific effect estimates; the Indonesian cohort of 69 patients and 96 eyes is single-centre in a tuberculosis-endemic setting where 41.7 percent of eyes were presumed infectious, so its proportions do not generalise to a low-prevalence setting; NO located anchor provides a scleritis-free comparison group for the uveitis outcome; and no located anchor reports whether concomitant uveitis in scleritis carries the same natural history, treatment response, or complication risk as uveitis occurring alone. Glaucoma and cataracts were reviewed and withheld as DUPLICATE-SCOPE: the registry already carries direct uveitis-to-glaucoma and uveitis-to-cataracts edges, so authoring either alongside this file's uveitis edge would register the same route twice at different indirection and add a direct-versus-chain redundancy conflict to the standing CRG review set, even though the same registry reports them as the most frequent complications of scleritis.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Presumed infectious scleritis, particularly tuberculosis-associated disease, which the located cohort reports at 41.7 percent of eyes in an endemic setting and which changes both the workup and the treatment pathway

Granulomatosis with polyangiitis, which the registry reports as the systemic disease with the significantly highest rate of ocular complications (p<0.0001) and which is a competing explanation for any scleritis-uveitis picture

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Rheumatoid arthritis is the systemic disease most consistently associated with scleritis, and the located evidence spans a population-based analysis of 10,939,823 patients, an EMR-wide review designed specifically to avoid referral bias, and a dedicated review of the rheumatoid ocular manifestations: the population-based United Kingdom analysis of 2,946 incident scleritis cases against 12,020 matched controls characterises scleritis as a disease whose defining epidemiology is its association with immune-mediated inflammatory disease, with adjustment for age, sex, deprivation index, race or ethnicity, smoking status, nation, and body mass index (PMID 33728815); a health-system-wide electronic-record analysis of all charts carrying systemic autoimmune and scleritis diagnoses states explicitly that prior series assessed the relationship between systemic autoimmune disorders and scleritis only in patients referred for rheumatology or ocular inflammation, which introduces referral bias, and that the EMR-wide review was conducted to determine the prevalence of both and which disorders carried the highest relative risk of developing scleritis (PMID 33407267); and a review of rheumatoid arthritis-associated ocular disease reports that scleritis and peripheral ulcerative keratitis are less common than dry eye disease but represent severe inflammatory complications generally requiring systemic immunosuppression, with escalation to biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs including tumour necrosis factor inhibitors and rituximab supported for refractory scleritis and corneal melt, though the evidence is described as largely observational (PMID 42122940); recorded as documented association only with the direction of the relationship stated explicitly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of rheumatoid arthritis is established for any individual, and the direction here is the reverse of the clinical sequence: in every located design the systemic disease is the antecedent and the ocular manifestation is the consequent, so the clinically operative arrow runs rheumatoid-arthritis to scleritis, and this edge is registered as the reciprocal view of that relationship rather than as a claim that scleritis produces rheumatoid arthritis. The located evidence does not permit even a clean reciprocal reading, because the health-system review reports only prevalence of co-diagnosis and relative risk of developing scleritis from the systemic side, and its own stated motivation is that prior work was referral-biased, which means the magnitude of any association is better estimated from the population anchor than from the ophthalmology-clinic literature. The dedicated rheumatoid-ocular review is a narrative synthesis rather than a pooled estimate, and it states plainly that the biologic-escalation evidence is largely observational. Individual claims require a dated rheumatoid arthritis diagnosis with serology, rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide status, disease activity measures, and a dated scleritis diagnosis, and the reviewing clinician should note that the temporal sequence runs from the systemic disease to the eye, not the reverse.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a shared systemic autoimmune driver in which the same dysregulated immune response that produces rheumatoid synovitis acts on the sclera, generating scleritis as an extra-articular manifestation; the located review frames dry eye disease as the most frequent ocular manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis and scleritis and peripheral ulcerative keratitis as less common but severe manifestations requiring systemic immunosuppression, which is consistent with scleritis being an extra-articular expression of the systemic disease rather than an independent ocular process, and the immune-mediated route is named as hypothesized because no located anchor demonstrates the effector pathway connecting rheumatoid synovitis to scleral inflammation.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at population-based-cohort, health-system-big-data, and narrative-review class, and deliberately at a framing that names the reverse arrow rather than burying it: the population anchor is registered as the association anchor because it is the only design that estimates the relationship without the referral bias the third anchor identifies (PMID 33728815); the health-system big-data anchor is registered specifically for its explicit statement that prior series assessed this relationship only in referred patients, which is the located justification for preferring the population estimate and is disclosed so a reviewer does not over-read ophthalmology-clinic figures (PMID 33407267); and the rheumatoid-ocular review supplies the extra-articular framing and the treatment implication, together with its own admission that the biologic-escalation evidence is largely observational (PMID 42122940). Because the sequence runs systemic-disease to eye, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, states the reverse direction in the causation status, and routes individual attribution through paired dated diagnoses with serology and activity measures.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The population anchor is the strongest design in this edge at 10,939,823 patients and 2,946 incident scleritis cases, but its located abstract reports design, cohort sizes, and the adjustment set rather than rheumatoid-arthritis-specific effect estimates, so the magnitude of this particular association cannot be quoted from these references; the health-system big-data anchor is a single integrated delivery system, which carries its own population-selection characteristic, and its located abstract reports the design and rationale without the resulting prevalence figures; the rheumatoid-ocular review is a narrative search rather than a systematic review with pooled estimates, and the located abstract reports only that dry eye disease is the most frequent manifestation, so no scleritis-specific frequency is available; NO located anchor reports the proportion of rheumatoid arthritis patients who develop scleritis, which is the denominator that would matter most for an individual claim; and no located anchor separates scleritis in seropositive from seronegative rheumatoid arthritis, which is the distinction that would determine whether the two are the same route. Dry eye disease was reviewed and withheld as TARGET-EXHAUSTION because the same review names it the most frequent ocular manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis, but the catalog carries no dry-eye identity of its own and dry-eye-syndrome already appears elsewhere in the registry under a different primary.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Seronegative rheumatoid arthritis and spondyloarthropathy, which the located Indonesian cohort identifies as a common non-infectious systemic associate of scleritis and which is a distinct disease requiring separate documentation
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis, which the scleritis registry reports as carrying the significantly highest rate of ocular complications (p<0.0001)
Ocular masquerade syndromes including ocular lymphoma, which mimic scleritis and must be excluded before any systemic attribution
Infectious scleritis, particularly tuberculosis-associated, which the located cohort reports at 41.7 percent of eyes in an endemic setting

The conservative framing states the reverse arrow openly, registers the referral-bias finding as the reason the population anchor is preferred, carries the narrative review's own admission that the biologic-escalation evidence is largely observational, and requires paired dated diagnoses with serology and activity measures rather than any claim of ocular-to-systemic causation.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Systemic lupus erythematosus is the second major systemic disease associated with scleritis, and the located evidence supplies the population-level association structure, the referral-bias correction, and a directly documented ocular manifestation: the population-based United Kingdom analysis of 2,946 incident scleritis cases against 12,020 matched controls estimates the associations of scleritis with immune-mediated inflammatory disease with multivariable adjustment for age, sex, deprivation, race or ethnicity, smoking, nation, and body mass index (PMID 33728815); the health-system-wide electronic-record review states that prior series assessed systemic autoimmune disorders in scleritis only in referred patients and corrects for that referral bias across all charts carrying both diagnoses (PMID 33407267); and a secondary cohort analysis of a population-based lupus cohort examines the risks of ophthalmic disorders in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, situating ocular involvement as a recognised complication of the systemic disease rather than an incidental association (PMID 32160869); recorded as documented association only, with the reverse direction stated and with the evidence density for this particular pair registered as lower than for the rheumatoid-arthritis pair rather than smoothed over.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of systemic lupus erythematosus is established for any individual, and as with the rheumatoid-arthritis edge the located sequence runs from the systemic disease to the eye, so this edge is the reciprocal view and not a claim that scleritis produces lupus. The evidence density for this pair is materially weaker than for the rheumatoid pair and that is stated rather than hidden: unlike the rheumatoid-arthritis edge, no located anchor in this edge reports a systemic-lupus-erythematosus-specific or scleritis-specific effect estimate in its located abstract, and none supplies a scleritis-free comparison group for the ocular outcome, so the edge rests on the population anchor's overall immune-mediated-inflammatory-disease association structure plus the existence of a dedicated ophthalmic-risk analysis in a lupus cohort rather than on a quantified pair-specific estimate. The located cohort analyses are also largely administrative, which limits clinical phenotyping of the scleritis subtype. Individual claims require a dated systemic lupus erythematosus diagnosis meeting contemporary classification criteria with relevant autoantibody profile and complement levels, organ involvement assessment, and a separately dated scleritis diagnosis, and the reviewing clinician should note that the temporal sequence runs from the systemic disease to the ocular manifestation.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a shared systemic autoimmune driver in which the same immune dysregulation that produces lupus multi-organ involvement extends to the sclera, generating scleritis as an extra-articular ocular manifestation; the located rhupus case literature, in which anterior scleritis presents alongside lupus nephritis, is consistent with this single systemic process expressing itself in the eye, and the ocular masquerade and infection alternatives must be excluded before any such attribution, because a scleritis in a patient with lupus may equally reflect treatment toxicity, opportunistic infection secondary to immunosuppression, or an unrelated ocular process, none of which is the hypothesised route.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at population-based-cohort, health-system-big-data, and lupus-cohort-analytic class, and registered at explicitly lower evidential density than this file's rank 2 edge, with that difference carried on the face of the edge rather than smoothed over: the population anchor supplies the association structure free of referral bias and is the anchor that makes the systemic association estimable at all (PMID 33728815); the health-system big-data anchor supplies the explicit correction of referral bias across all charts carrying both diagnoses (PMID 33407267); and the lupus ophthalmic-risk cohort analysis supplies the located evidence that ophthalmic disorder risk in systemic lupus is itself a studied, quantified phenomenon, which is what makes the association clinically coherent rather than incidental (PMID 32160869). Because no located anchor reports a pair-specific effect estimate, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, names the reverse arrow, requires full classification-criteria documentation on the lupus side, and requires exclusion of treatment toxicity and opportunistic infection before the shared-driver route is accepted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No located anchor in this edge reports a systemic-lupus-erythematosus-specific or scleritis-specific association estimate in its abstract, so unlike the rheumatoid-arthritis edge this one cannot be quantified from its references, and a reviewer should treat the effect size as unestablished rather than assume it approximates the rheumatoid figure; the population anchor's located abstract reports design, cohort sizes, and adjustment rather than pair-specific results; the health-system big-data anchor is a single integrated delivery system and its located abstract reports rationale rather than outcome figures; the lupus ophthalmic-risk analysis is a secondary cohort analysis of a population-based cohort, so it estimates ophthalmic risk within a lupus cohort and does not estimate scleritis risk within a general population, which is the opposite conditioning from what this edge's direction implies; no located anchor supplies a scleritis-free comparison group for the lupus outcome; and no located anchor separates scleritis attributable to active lupus from scleritis attributable to lupus treatment, including corticosteroid or mycophenolate toxicity and immunosuppression-associated infection.
